ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et contre le financement du terrorisme); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the central register of beneficial owners (Loi du 13 janvier 2019 créant le registre des bénéficiaires effectifs); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2019 on the organisation of the Register; CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on anti-money laundering; Luxembourg law of 25 March 2020 amending the 2004 AML Act and creating the Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or EU national identity card for every ultimate beneficial owner (each natural person with 25% or more of rights or control)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National identity/passport authority of the UBO's country of residency (e.g., Ministry of Interior, police, consular post)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if the origin state is party to the 1961 Apostille Convention) or consular legalization via the Luxembourg embassy/consulate in the origin state; otherwise recognized notarization; shall be accompanied by sworn translation into French or German if not issued in one of these languages

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or certificate of incorporation for each corporate shareholder, partner, or indirect corporate parent (in the SCSp chain)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of Commerce and Companies of the country of incorporation (for Luxembourg corporate partners, the RCS; for foreign partners, the equivalent official company registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization (depending on the origin country) + official French/German translation; Luxembourg-issued documents need only the RCS extract

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Legalized copy of the constitutive documents and shareholder/partner register of the direct corporate partner(s), including complete UBO chain and ownership percentages up to 25% or above
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered office agent or corporate counsel of the partner entity; for Luxembourg partners, a notarized excerpt from the notarial deed files
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille/consular legalization for non-Luxembourg origin; if the partner is Luxembourg-incorporated, a certified notarial copy issued by the Luxembourg notary in whose minutes the corporate acts are filed

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and six-month source-of-funds proof (bank statements, loan agreement, or audited accounts) covering all initial contributions and any undertakings regarding future capital calls
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Correspondent bank of the investor or the financing institution retaining the account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank notarized signature of the account manager (apostille not required for bank documents in many cases, but if required by the Luxembourg AML officer, the signature is notarized and apostilled/consularized)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate / certificate of non-conviction for all individuals qualifying as PEPs (politically exposed persons) and for all UBOs if the domestic law of the residence state so requires; otherwise an express negative PEP declaration under Luxembourg AML forms
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Judicial records office / criminal records bureau of the UBO's country of residence (casier judiciaire)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization + sworn translation into French or German; the certificate must be issued not more than three months before submission to the notary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, partners, and authorised representatives against the United Nations Security Council sanctions lists, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List (as a prudent benchmark for USD-corridor banks), Luxembourg (Ministry of Finance / FIU) national freezes list, and the World Bank Implied Sanctions List. Independent PEP determination is performed under the Law of 12 November 2004, art. 3(6)-(8), and CSSF Regulation 12-02, requiring continuous risk-based monitoring, enhanced due diligence for high-risk third-country PEPs, and immediate reporting to the Luxembourg FIU of any suspicious transaction or attempted transaction. A permanent fact-check against LBR, BEE, and external commercial databases (Dow Jones, Refinitiv, World-Check) is recommended. All cleared files must be retained for five years after the business relationship ends (article 6-1 of the 2004 Act).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (lbr.lu) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), electronic pre-filing portal and negative certificate application interface
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name of an SCSp must be expressed in the Latin alphabet; if the name is in a non-Latin script (e.g., Chinese, Arabic, Cyrillic), a phonetic Latin transliteration and an official French/German/English translation are mandatory for RCS registration. The RCS accepts names in French, German, Luxembourgish, or English, provided the name complies with the rule of lexicitæ and clearly contains or is followed by the legal-form indicator 'SCSp' (Société en Commandite Spéciale). All official filings and notarial deeds must be drafted in French, German, or Luxembourgish (a deed in English is permissible if the notary certifies an authentic translation in French or German).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: BANQUE / BANK (authorization by the Luxembourg Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier required)
ASSURANCE / INSURANCE (authorization by the Commissariat aux Assurances required)
FONDS DE PENSION / PENSION FUND (CSSF notification required)
SICAV, SIF, FCP, SICAR (specific regulated investment vehicle forms reserved for licenced funds)
STATE / ÉTAT / GOUVERNEMENT / MINISTRE (only usable with ministerial consent)
COMMUNE / MUNICIPALITY (authorization from the Ministry of the Interior required)
UNION EUROPÉENNE / EUROPEAN UNION (specific Commission approval required)
CROIX-ROUGE / RED CROSS (reserved to the Luxembourg Red Cross and its chapters)
OFFICE / CHAMBRE (if it implies a public-law body, prior approval required)
POSTE / POSTAL (only authorised operators within the meaning of the Postal Services Act)
ARMÉE / DEFENSE (Ministry of Defence authorization required)
VERT / ENVIRONNEMENT (only for entities with the qualifying environmental certification/licence)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon receiving an RCS negative certificate refusal (refus de certificat de non-confusion), the applicant must obtain the written reasons for rejection from the RCS registry officer (curateur). The applicant has two administrative remedies: (i) within five business days, file a new name reservation addressing the suspensive grounds (e.g., modifying confusingly similar terms or deleting a forbidden token) via lbr.lu / RCS e-filing; (ii) if the rejection is based on a substantive interpretation of statutory name rules, submit an administrative appeal to the Director of the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés within one month of notification. A subsequent judicial appeal may be lodged before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (Chambre commerciale) within 40 days of the administrative refusal; legal representation by a Luxembourg avocet à la Cour is mandatory for any judicial appeal. If the applicant does not file an appeal and the 30-day reservation expires, the name returns to the public pool, but a fresh application for the same name may be filed after a 10-day cool-off period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office (domiciliation service) is acceptable solely as an administrative mailing address and for the convenience of service of process, but is not suffisant for the manufacturing activity. For ISIC 1079 self-heating instant meal production, the entity must maintain in Luxembourg a physical production facility and a staffed place of effective management. The ALVA (Administration luxembourgeoise vétérinaire et alimentaire) will require a verifiable operational site for the food-manufacturing licence, and the tax administration may challenge utilisation of a virtual office if commercial substance is otherwise absent. Consequently, a virtual office can be used only as a temporary pre-incorporation accommodation and must be replaced by a real operational lease before the initial licence application is approved.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 85% – the likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection by ALVA or the Labour and Mines Inspectorate (ITM) within the first 12 months of licence activation is assessed at 85%; a pre-licensing mandatory on-site inspection by ALVA occurs before any food-manufacturing registration is issued. The ITM can also inspect premises without notice to verify employee health and safety (HACCP implementation), and the Luxembourg tax authorities (ACD) may perform physical substance audits where a manufacturing SCSp is beneficiary of treaty benefits. Therefore, permanent and substantive local presence is a compliance prerequisite.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Civil-law notary in Luxembourg (Notaire de langue française)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Amended Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 318-1 et seq., as introduced by the Law of 23 July 2016; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies, as amended
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg City
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Constitutive deed / partnership agreement (contrat de société / statuts) lodged electronically with the RCS and published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for an SCSp; contributions are freely determined in the partnership agreement, may be cash or in-kind, and no blocked escrow account or bank certificate is required; the general partner is jointly and severally liable for partnership debts, while limited partners are liable only up to their committed contribution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTIONS OF THE SOLE GENERAL PARTNER OF [●] S.C.Sp. ADOPTED ON [DATE]

1. The articles of association of the partnership are approved and adopted in final form.
2. The general partner subscribes to its capital contribution, and the partnership interests set out in the contribution schedule are allotted.
3. The registered office is fixed at [street, number, postcode, city], Luxembourg, subject to communications to the RCS and the revenue authorities.
4. [Name], identified by passport [No.], is appointed as Gérant, with sole power to manage, administer and represent the partnership, within the limits of the corporate purpose.
5. Due authorisation is granted for the lodging of the articles at the RCS, for publication in the RESA, and for all ancillary filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Constitutive Deed (Articles of Association) of the SCSp
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (if real estate is contributed or voluntary notarisation) or the partners acting by private deed; no prior administrative clearance required for incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the partnership agreement in French, German or English; a French version must be filed with the RCS and an English translation may be attached. The deed must state the legal form (S.C.Sp.), corporate name, registered office address, corporate purpose, duration, identity of the general partner, identity of the limited partners and their capital commitments, classes of partnership interests, transfer restrictions and the powers of the Gérant. Have all partners sign the deed in original and complete the contribution schedule; if real estate is contributed, the deed must be executed before a notary. Retain the executed original for RCS lodgment.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association (statuts)
Contribution and subscription schedule with commitment amounts
Copy of passport or national ID of the general partner and each limited partner
Proof of availability of the registered office address (occupancy title or domiciliation agreement)
Criminal record extract (bulletin no. 3) and residence documents for the Gérant
Bank confirmation of cash contributions, where applicable
Corporate resolution of the general partner, if the general partner is a legal entity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any defect by executing a rectificative deed (acte rectificatif) and re-file before the RCS deadline indicated in the query letter; pay any supplementary filing or publication fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Lodgment of the Constitutive Deed with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed constitutive deed and supporting exhibits through the LBR e-filing portal. Attach scanned copies of the deed, identification documents, registered office acceptance letter and proof of payment of the official fees (75 EUR RCS registration fee plus 19 EUR RESA publication fee). A Luxembourg lawyer, notary or accountant holding an e-filing mandate may lodge the filing on behalf of the partnership. Ensure the beneficial ownership declaration data for the RBE register are consistent with the filed deed.
required_dossiers: Original or certified electronic copy of the constitutive deed
RCS filing form (formulaire de dépôt)
Identity documents of all signatories or of the authorised filing agent
Power of attorney granted to the filing agent, where applicable
Registered office consent letter (accord du domiciliataire)
Receipt of payment of 75 EUR + 19 EUR official fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or a notice of inadmissibility, cure the identified defect by filing a rectificative deed within the time limit stated in the notice, re-lodge the corrected instrument and pay any additional filing fee; if rejected for incompleteness, resubmit with the requested documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration, Issuance of Business Number (Matricule) and RESA Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers, Central RCS Office, Luxembourg City
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After substantive review, the RCS allocates the registration number (matricule), enters the SCSp into the trade register and forwards the deed to the RESA official electronic gazette for publication. Legal personality and contractual capacity commence upon registration of the deed; verify the accuracy of the publisRS entry. File the beneficial ownership declaration with the RBE register within one month of registration.
required_dossiers: Official filing certificate issued by the RCS
RCS extract (extrait du RCS) after registration
Proof of RESA publication
Beneficial ownership declaration submitted to the RBE register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If errors appear in the registered entry or the RESA publication, file a written rectification request with the RCS attaching the correct data; the RCS will publish an erratum in the RESA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT and Social Security Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) and Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, verify that the business matricule is recorded and file the VAT activation declaration with the AEDT to obtain a Luxembourg VAT number (LU…) if taxable supplies will be made in the partnership's own name. Register all staff, including the Gérant, with the CCSS and secure compulsory occupational accident insurance. The SCSp is fiscally transparent for income tax purposes but remains a taxable person for VAT where relevant. Confirm any optional election for corporate income tax treatment with the tax advisor.
required_dossiers: RCS extract and matricule certificate
Copy of the constitutive deed and RESA publication
Identity and professional details of the Gérant
VAT registration form (forms 300/306) submitted to the AEDT
CCSS employer registration forms and employee declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT registration is delayed or queried, respond via the myGuichet secured mailbox with the requested economic activity evidence; in case of refusal, lodge an appeal with the Director of the AEDT within the statutory deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Commencement Application for the Business Establishment Permit (Autorisation d'Établissement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction générale des classes moyennes (Ministry of the Economy, SME Department), through the Guichet unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before commencing manufacture of self-heating instant meals, submit the application for the business establishment permit under the amended Law of 2 September 2011 on access to the professions of artisan, trader, industrialist and certain liberal professions. Attach proof of professional qualification of the Gérant or the responsible production manager, the criminal record extract, RCS extract, bank details and a description of the industrial site. The permit is personal to the applicant and site-specific; it must be obtained before the first employment contract or commercial activity.
required_dossiers: Application form for the autorisation d'établissement
RCS extract of the SCSp
Criminal record extract (bulletin no. 3) of the manager
Evidence of professional competence or diploma in food technology / industrial management
Detailed business plan and production process description
Lease or occupancy title for the industrial premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is refused, lodge a hierarchical appeal (recours gracieux) within three months and, if necessary, a judicial appeal before the Administrative Tribunal; alternatively, remedy the qualification deficiency by appointing a qualified operational director and resubmit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction générale des classes moyennes (business establishment permit) jointly with the Administration vétérinaire et alimentaire (AVA) for food business approval
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (business establishment permit) and Food Business Establishment Approval issued under Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 and the amended Law of 2 September 2011

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Environment Agency of Luxembourg), Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – mandatory EIA screening (simplified impact notice) under the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment, Annex II class 7 (food-products industry); a full EIA is required where processing capacities exceed the food-industry threshold (animal raw materials > 75 t/day or vegetable raw materials > 300 t/day), where Seveso III-listed hazardous substances are stored above lower-tier thresholds, or where the site is located in or near protected zones.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Process wastewater must be pre-treated to comply with the amended Law of 19 December 2008 on water management and the applicable Grand-Ducal regulation on industrial wastewater discharges (typical discharge limits to municipal sewers: COD ≤ 125 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 25 mg/L, TSS ≤ 35 mg/L, pH 6–8.5). Air emissions, steam and odour abatement must comply with the Industrial Emissions Directive 2010/75/EU as transposed by the amended Law of 9 May 2014. Spent exothermic packets and food waste must be managed under the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management, using pre-authorised waste carriers and documented duty of care.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Local commune fire safety and occupancy clearance following inspection by the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS); industrial building authorisation (autorisation de construire) and operating occupancy permit from the commune; occupational safety and health clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM), including the mandatory risk assessment (document unique), machinery safety inspection, personal protective equipment programme, emergency response and evacuation drills, and compliant storage of exothermic reactants under the Labor Code, REACH and CLP regulations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) — Direct Tax Authority (Luxembourg, 33 rue de Gasperich, L-5826 Hesperange; portal: myguichet.lu); Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) — VAT & Registration Authority (Boulevard Prince Henri, L-1724 Luxembourg; e-file via eTVA portal, managed within MyGuichet.lu).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Phase 1: Foreign/investor entities must first appoint a Luxembourg-resident Réviseur d'Entreprises Agréé and a registered local tax representative (for non-EU principals) prior to VAT registration. Phase 2: File incorporation/registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via a certified notary; the RCS automatically transmits the corporate data to the AEDT. Phase 3: Upon RCS registration, the entity receives a 13-digit national identification number (N° d'identification — matricule), which is simultaneously used as the direct-tax TIN. Phase 4: For VAT, submit the eTVA registration form (Formulaire 1/2 — Déclaration de commencement d'activité) through the RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) compliance step; the AEDT issues a distinct VAT number with prefix 'LU' followed by 8 digits. Phase 5: For an SCSp (SOPARFI variant not relevant; pure SCSp), the transparent entity itself registers for VAT when it sells supplies in its own name; otherwise, the general partner (associé gérant) may register on behalf of the partnership. Phase 6: Required submission of statutory articles, proof of beneficial owner filing (RBE), EU VAT status certificate (if claiming prior business), and a statement of intended commercial activities in Luxembourg. Processing time: 5–15 business days for TIN; 1–3 weeks for VAT ID.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible. The SCSp (Société en Commandite Spéciale) is, by default, treated as tax-transparent (fiscally transparent) for Luxembourg income tax purposes. It is not itself a taxable person for CIT and city business tax (WIR); its partners — both general and limited — are directly subject to income tax (IRC or IRPP) on their respective shares of the SCSp's income. For VAT, however, the SCSp is considered a taxable person (assujetti) when it independently supplies goods/services, consistent with the EU VAT Directive principle that fiscally transparent partnerships may be liable for VAT in their own name for the activities they conduct. The manufacturing activity (ISIC 1079 self-heating meals) executed by the SCSp is thus directly attributed to the partners for income tax, while the VAT liability sits at the partnership level.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: (i) Non-transparent election: The SCSp may irrevocably elect to be treated as a taxable entity for Luxembourg income tax purposes (option for corporate taxation), transforming the partnership into a fiscal subject akin to a capital company (ruling from the ACD required); once elected, the SCSp is subject to CIT at 17% (2025), municipal business tax (WIR), contribution to employment fund (7¢ top-up), and the solidarity surcharge. (ii) Partial transparency hybrid check: Luxembourg's transposition of ATAD (Article 4) provides an optional 'step-down' approach under controlled-foreign-company rules that can align the SCSp's transparency with a partner's home jurisdiction classification — a de-facto check-the-box function for cross-border investors. (iii) Partnership audit election: Under Luxembourg general tax law, the partners may elect (via filing of the common partnership return) that the SCSp's accounts be reviewed at partnership level for determination of distributed shares, creating binding effect on the tax authorities. (iv) Hybrid mismatch adjustments: Where a partner's home jurisdiction treats the SCSp as opaque, Luxembourg will apply the ATAD anti-hybrid rules, requiring an election to re-characterise the SCSp's income under the 'same-country' exception.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms_note: No US-style comprehensive check-the-box election exists under Luxembourg law; transparency is the statutory default, with a one-way corporate-taxation opt-in requiring prior ACD approval and a clear commercial rationale.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.legal_reference: Articles 1–2 and 3 of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (Loi du 4 décembre 1967); Circular L.I.R. n° 14/4 (SCSp fiscal transparency); Law of 12 July 2013 introducing the SCSp; ATAD Law of 21 December 2017 (anti-hybrid); AEDT Circular 760 (VAT treatment of transparent partnerships); VAT Law of 12 February 1979 (Articles 2–4, 26, 57).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée; TVA) — Luxembourg EU VAT system; administered by the AEDT; Council Directive 2006/112/EC implemented via national VAT Law of 12 February 1979.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: €35,000 annual taxable turnover (small-business exemption, Article 57 VAT Law) — where the SCSp's worldwide supplies within Luxembourg do not exceed EUR 35,000 per annum, the entity may be exempt from VAT with no input VAT recovery; forming part of a VAT group overrides the threshold. Cross-border manufacturing and export activities above this threshold require mandatory EU-Article-214 registration. No business-to-consumer distance-selling threshold applies within Luxembourg (single EU regime from 2021 under VAT e-commerce package with EUR 10,000 EU-wide threshold). Zero-rated and exempt-with-credit supplies count toward the threshold; physically exported goods are excluded. Registration is mandatory from the first euro if the entity makes intra-EU acquisitions above EUR 10,000 or holds a VAT-group election.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2G e-invoicing via PEPPOL (since 2023 for larger contracts, fully effective 2024). No real-time fiscal clearance (no 'VAT live' reporting) — the Luxembourg system applies periodic digital VAT return filing (monthly, quarterly, or annually depending on turnover) via the eTVA portal. Standard B2B e-invoicing is voluntary in Luxembourg; the Government has committed to transposing the EU ViDA / standard e-invoicing mandate by 2028 (draft bill under preparation). Digital stamping of invoices is not used in Luxembourg. VAT filing is mandatory digitally for all registered persons. A full SAF-T (Standard Audit File – Tax) upload must accompany periodic returns for taxpayers with turnover exceeding EUR 50,000 (requested electronically by AEDT). Integration API: MyGuichet.lu and the AEDT system allow machine-to-machine submission of VAT returns and SAF-T via authenticated API for large ERP users.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.standard_reduced_rates: 14% intermediate, 8% reduced, 3% super-reduced (2025 rates); self-heating packaged meals (ISIC 1079 — processed food) qualify for the super-reduced 3% rate when supplied for human consumption (Article 39, 7° VAT Law); the standard 17% rate applies to the industrial manufacturing input supplies and any non-food items.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.vital_nexus_rule: Plain intra-EU physical presence nexus applies; an SCSp with no Luxembourg substance but treasury-management or manufacturing activities subcontracted locally obtains VAT registration purely through the place-of-supply rules for goods (Art. 31 VAT Law) if domestic storage exists. Without fixed establishment, manufacture in Luxembourg through contract manufacturers is attributed to the principal for VAT purposes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.filing_and_payment_calendar: Quarterly returns (turnover ≤ EUR 2,000,000); monthly returns (turnover > EUR 2,000,000); annual return for exempt persons. Payments due by the 15th of the following month (monthly filers); quarterly payment with 1-month extension — the Luxembourg AEDT has late-interest rules of 0.8% per month on late VAT, plus penalties up to 10% of the due tax, and criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 for wilful failure to file.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: An SCSp manufacturing self-heating instant meals in Luxembourg may apply the 0% VAT rate for (i) goods shipped to non-EU destinations (Article 162 VAT Law — export of goods outside the EU); (ii) intra-EU supplies to taxable persons in other Member States (Article 170 VAT Law — intra-Community supplies, including a valid customer VAT number and INTRASTAT where applicable); and (iii) the export of services directly linked to export (including freight, insurance, loading services) per Article 149 VAT Law. The zero-rating is strictly conditioned on: economic movement of goods leaving the EU within 90 days of invoice (customs export declaration accepted); the seller's documentation providing full traceable chain of custody (manufacturer → carrier → exit customs post); and the buyer being identifiable as a taxable or non-resident party. For the specific cargo 'Instant Hot Water Self-Heating Pot' (exothermic reaction packaging — CaO quicklime/water reaction), the product qualifies as generically manufactured goods; no special export authorization beyond general export control is needed since it contains no dual-use hazardous quantity of calcium oxide (nett content of exothermic material ≤ 100 g per unit). For intra-Community supply, the SCSp must verify the customer's valid VAT ID in VIES and, if the goods are shipped by the SCSp itself, report the transport in its own records with CMR/airway bill.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD — Single Administrative Document; Exit Summary Declaration when no full declaration is required; submitted via Luxembourg Customs (LU Customs, part of AEDT for IPR regimes) in the NCTS computerised transit system)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (showing exporter of record = SCSp, consignee = foreign buyer, and vessel/flight dates)
Commercial Invoice (with full description of goods, harmonised system code 2106.90 / 3824.99, unit value, Incoterms, country of origin 'LU')

Inward Remittance Certificate (documented proof via the SWIFT MT-103 wire transfer that the export proceeds have been repatriated to the SCSp's Luxembourg bank account or the partner's account if treasury is centralised at partner level) — required by ACD practice to substantiate the underlying commercial reality where the exporting entity is a transparent partnership with non-resident partners; recommended alternative when the beneficiary is the parent partner: a certified treasury consolidation statement from the group auditor

Proof of Physical Transit (CMR waybill for road export, ferry/air cargo manifests, container seal records, or terminal gate-out stamp showing the goods physically left the EU customs territory within the 90-day period)

Packing List (to certify that each self-heating pot contains a food-grade exothermic reactable mass of ≤ 100 g of calcium oxide, meeting the unregulated safety threshold, and to allow customs inspection)

Export License / General Export Authorisation (for self-heating meal products with no dual-use classification: a GEA-FLEX or EXTRACOM number to be referenced on the customs declaration; for any quantity of exothermic material above the 100 g threshold, a dual-use export-authorisation check is required per EU Regulation 2021/821, potentially requiring a prior authorization)
Certificate of Origin (certificate EUR.1 or REX declaration if the buyer claims a preferential tariff, or a non-preferential origin declaration in any case)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Luxembourg AEDT and Customs Authority jointly enforce export zero-rating. Audit triggers include: (i) serial or low-value exports to sanctioned territories, (ii) inconsistent bill-of-lading quantities versus freight manifests (commonly exploited with heat-reactive goods where chemical weight shifts at customs checkpoint), and (iii) SCSp entities with non-resident partners operating in high-volume consumer-goods sectors. Where zero-rating is rejected, the EUR fiscal creditor issues a VAT correction assessing 17% VAT on the full export value plus default interest of 0.8% per month (legal interest regime, Article 23 VAT Law) and a late-payment penalty of 5% at the time of assessment rising to 1% per additional month (max 20%). In cases of intentional falsification of transport documents or over-declaration of exothermic-material compliance, the penalties escalate: administrative fines up to EUR 250,000 (Article 60 VAT Law), criminal fines up to double the evaded tax, and imprisonment of managers in serious cases (Luxembourg Criminal Code Article 60bis/contextual VAT fraud provisions). Additionally, the customs authorities may impose a breach of customs-export controls (EUR 1,500 per false declaration) and suspend the exporter's authorised-economy-operator status. Clawback mechanics: an AEDT reassessment within a five-year statutory limitation period (which is extended to 10 years in cases involving intentional fraud or documentary forgery) automatically lifts the underlying VAT deductibility of the input costs and reclassifies the export supply as taxable; the partnership's partners (jointly and severally; Article 47 VAT Law) become personally liable for the VAT, interest, and penalties. In a cross-border structure, the clawback can further trigger non-deductibility of the foreign partner's share under hybrid-mismatch rules if the partner's jurisdiction has treated the SCSp as opaque, creating a second layer of taxation.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.practical_compliance_note: For ISIC 1079 self-heating food, the Luxembourg Customs require that the exothermic material is declared under the correct CN-coded subheading (TB 3824 9919 if using quicklime/water, or CN 2106 90 if the reaction is part of the food composition); a mismatch with the commercial invoice description is the single most frequent reason for disallowed zero-rating. The SCSp should implement an e-export-dossier system that automatically collates the SAD + shipping documents + payment trace for each consignment within 180 days.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: European Central Bank (ECB) within the Eurosystem, with the Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) acting as the national central bank and operational agent for TARGET2 and balance-of-payments statistics; prudential banking supervision is co-exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). Luxembourg maintains no separate exchange-control administration and no Ministry-of-Finance FX licensing body for euro or freely convertible currency operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility on both current and capital accounts. Luxembourg is a Eurozone Member State and grants unrestricted cross-border capital movements under Article 63 TFEU. There are no exchange-control authorizations, prior-approval regimes, conversion quotas, or currency bands applicable to equity injections, profit remittances, dividend distributions, loan repayments, trade payments, or repatriation of liquidation proceeds. The only operational filters are EU/UN sanctions screening, the AML/CFT Law of 12 November 2004 (as amended), and CSSF prudential obligations imposed on the depository bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender requirement: export proceeds must not be repatriated within any mandatory timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio applies to export receipts. The SCSp may lawfully retain USD or CNY receivables in foreign-currency accounts held with a Luxembourg credit institution without BCL authorization. The applicable administrative requirements are limited to balance-of-payments statistical reporting by the bank (per Regulation (EC) No 184/2005), Intrastat/CN coding for EU trade, transfer-of-funds traceability under Regulation (EU) 2023/1113, and, where the exothermic reaction composition contains controlled precursors, export licensing under the EU Dual-Use Regulation (EU) 2021/821.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational current account (EUR) with segregated trade-finance and escrow sub-accounts
Operational account and Capital Escrow Account (dépôt-escrow) for partner contributions
Operational corporate account with documentary-credit trade facilities
Operational account (partnership eligibility assessed individually on commercial substance)
Capital Escrow / funds-services account for UBO-protected capital positioning

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium. Luxembourg authorizes a modest number of payment institutions and electronic money institutions under PSD2 and the Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services, and EEA EMIs may passport into Luxembourg; however, most automated or offshore digital EMIs design their onboarding for incorporated legal entities and fail to accommodate a Société en Commandite Spéciale, which has no legal personality. Legal constraints are: (i) the EMI must be authorized by the CSSF or passport under PSD2 with a Luxembourg notice; (ii) the SCSp can only act through its general partner (associé commandité), requiring a formal mandate and legal opinion; (iii) client funds must be safeguarded through segregation with an EU credit institution; (iv) an EMI is not permitted to issue Commercial Letters of Credit, act as escrow agent, or provide prime-brokerage liquidity. Recommended architecture: maintain core liquidity and all LC/escrow operations at a Tier-1 Luxembourg credit institution and use a passported EU EMI only for low-value, high-frequency TT operational wires where the reduced service envelope is acceptable.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not a statutory condition for corporate account opening in Luxembourg. CSSF Circular 12/552 (as amended) permits remote video-identification and reliance on certified copies where the credit institution applies equivalent risk-mitigation controls. In current Tier-1 bank practice, the general partner's authorized director must complete a recorded video interview, and the founding partner or its UBO must be identified remotely if EEA-resident; a notarized extract of the SCSp partnership deed and apostilled corporate documents for the general partner are required. Full in-person attendance at a Luxembourg branch is normally waived for EEA-resident signatories but may be demanded where any UBO resides in a high-risk third country or where the partner structure contains opaque intermediate entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp lacks legal personality; the bank's automated onboarding engine rejects the structure and relationship management contests the capacity of the partnership to hold the account in its own name.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg legal opinion citing the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended by the Law of 23 July 2016, confirming the SCSp is a partnership without legal personality but with contractual and treasury capacity; notarial deed of formation; executed partnership agreement; board resolution of the general partner appointing signatories; CSSF-beneficial reference to partnership accounts; account title styled 'SCSp [name], acting through its general partner [GP name]'.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commercial substance red flag: an SCSp is predominantly used as a tax-transparent investment vehicle, whereas the declared activity of manufacturing and distributing exothermic self-heating meals suggests operational inconsistency and potential round-tripping.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed toll-manufacturing agreements with the ISIC 1079 producer; purchase orders and distributor contracts; warehouse lease in Luxembourg or EEA if inventory is held; payroll and social-security records; Luxembourg VAT registration and periodic returns; projected cash-flow statements and normalized financial projections; written commercial rationale confirming the SCSp centralizes procurement, logistics, and international invoicing while manufacturing remains contracted out.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership transparency: a missing, incomplete, or stale registration in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) constitutes a hard rejection trigger and criminal exposure for the general partner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RBE extract or registration certificate dated within 30 days prior to onboarding identifying all natural-person UBOs; chain-of-ownership diagrams; passport or national ID copies; declaration of the general partner attesting accuracy; written undertaking to update the RBE and the bank within 30 days of any UBO change as mandated by the Law of 13 January 2019.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds and source-of-wealth alerts on initial partner capital contributions, particularly where a non-EEA corporate partner or private founder injects equity without a documented economic trail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of upstream bank statements for each contributing partner; audited or certified financial statements of corporate partners; source-of-wealth letter; FATCA/CRS self-certifications for the SCSp and all partners; negative PEP and sanctions screening results; bank reference letter from the contributor's home financial institution; capital subscription ledger matching the amounts to the partnership deed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Product and sector screening alerts: self-heating exothermic packs contain substances potentially subject to EU Dual-Use Regulation (EU) 2021/821, REACH (Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006), or hazardous-goods classification, causing the bank's transaction-monitoring engine to freeze the account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid Safety Data Sheets (SDS) for all chemical inputs; dual-use classification memorandum confirming no Annex I-listed substance is present; ECHA REACH registration numbers and supplier declarations; certificates of origin; completed bank export-control questionnaire; HS-coded commercial invoices and full Incoterms statements in each trade instruction; itinerary and logistics documentation for overseas shipments.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Partner capital contributions are routed by SWIFT MT103 or ISO 20022 pacs.008 with full payer and beneficiary identification as required by Regulation (EU) 2023/1113; the remittance narrative must state 'Capital contribution - SCSp [name], subscription agreement dated [date]' and reference the bank-assigned capital account. For euro injections, clearing occurs in TARGET2 via the BCL using the SCSp's Luxembourg IBAN; non-EUR funds are converted at the bank's spot rate or held in a separate foreign-currency sub-account. The bank will verify the contribution against the subscribed capital schedule and may require the BCL balance-of-payments statistical code 'Direct Investment - Equity Capital' under Regulation (EC) No 184/2005 for transactions at or above EUR 12,500. No regulatory approval is required, but third-country contributions are pre-screened for sanctions, AML/CFT, and source-of-wealth corroboration where the ultimate donor is a non-EEA resident.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails for supplier payments covering exothermic packs, aluminum self-heating containers, and packaging materials are: (i) SWIFT MT103 / ISO 20022 pacs.008 (TT payment) for advances and settlement amounts below the documentary-credit threshold, with reference to invoice number, Incoterms, and HS codes (e.g., HS 2106.90 for prepared meals, HS 7615/7323 for containers); (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit issued under UCP600, irrevocable and usually confirmed by the beneficiary's bank in Asia, for bulk high-value procurements; (iii) documentary collection (D/P or D/A) for mid-value transactions where LC confirmation charges are not economical; (iv) SEPA Credit Transfers for intra-EEA euro payments; and (v) TARGET2/RTGS same-day urgent wires. No domestic FX license or ministerial payment approval applies to outbound trade payments; the bank retains the right to demand export-control declarations before release of funds to third-country beneficiaries.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/CNY, EUR/GBP) executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or Luxembourg master agreement with a licensed EEA credit institution
FX swaps (spot-forward combinations) for short-term treasury rebalancing among EUR, USD, and CNY balances
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on offshore Renminbi (CNH) and other partially convertible emerging-market currencies
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for long-dated USD or CNY supplier contracts involving periodic exchange of principal and interest
OTC FX options, including vanilla puts/calls and zero-premium collars, for budget certainty on procurement currencies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing (dépôt des comptes annuels) with Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of financial year-end; default calendar year ending 31 December => filing due by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fines up to €1,500 per day; after repeated non-compliance, entity may be administratively struck-off and dissolved

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial owner confirmation (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs, RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval of annual accounts; if no approval is required, within one month after the anniversary of initial RBE registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to €12,500; criminal penalties including imprisonment for serious non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Partnership income tax return (Form 900/920 – corporate income tax, municipal business tax, net wealth tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 May for the preceding tax year; e-filing extension frequently granted to 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of 10% of assessed tax, monthly default interest of 0.8%, and additional administrative fines

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit required if the entity exceeds two of three criteria: balance sheet total above €4.4 million; net turnover above €8.8 million; average employees above 50 (per Luxembourg law implementing EU Directive 2013/34/EU).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 on companies' accounts; IFRS as adopted by the EU permitted for non-listed partnerships or required for listed entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must annually confirm the accuracy of beneficial owner information with the RBE. Any transfer of partnership interests or change in beneficial ownership must be reflected in the register and filed with RBE within 15 days of the event. The annual confirmation is an independent declaration, not a re-filing of the register, and must be signed by a legal representative.
